title: Beyond Correctness: Attribution of Natural-Language Documentation for Formal Libraries
abstract: arXiv:2610.33094v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Formal languages are widely used in software engineering to specify and verify program properties. Because their mathematical notation and logic are hard to read, developers often rely on natural-language documentation to understand the functions in formal libraries. Yet a documentation statement can be provably true and still hold after the function's behavior changes. We call a statement's dependence on the function's specific behavior attribution, and we give a method to check it. We design and implement DocAuth, a documentation-generation method that uses attribution to decide what to publish and attaches to each published sentence the formal property recovered from it, together with checkable evidence. On 150 functions from the Community Books library of the ACL2 theorem prover, three large language models produce proved but non-attributable properties for about a third of the functions. DocAuth matches or exceeds the attribution

translated_title: 超越正确性：形式化库自然语言文档的归因
translated_abstract: 形式化语言在软件工程中被广泛用于规约和验证程序性质。由于其数学符号和逻辑难以阅读，开发者通常依赖自然语言文档来理解形式化库中的函数。然而，一条文档陈述即使在函数行为发生改变后，仍可能被证明为真且依然成立。我们将陈述对函数特定行为的依赖性称为“归因”，并给出了一种检验归因的方法。我们设计并实现了 DocAuth——一种文档生成方法，它利用归因来决定发布哪些内容，并为每个发布的句子附加从中恢复出的形式化性质以及可检查的证据。在 ACL2 定理证明器 Community Books 库的 150 个函数上，三个大语言模型为约三分之一的函数生成了已证明但不可归因的性质。DocAuth 的归因表现与之相当或更优。
tldr: 该论文提出“归因”概念以检验文档陈述是否真正依赖于函数的特定行为，并实现了 DocAuth 文档生成方法，通过过滤掉已证明但不可归因的性质，并为每句发布的文档附加可检查的形式化证据，从而提升形式化库自然语言文档的可信度。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "attribution" to check whether a documentation statement genuinely depends on a function's specific behavior, and implements DocAuth, a documentation-generation method that filters out proved-but-non-attributable properties and attaches checkable formal evidence to each published sentence, improving the trustworthiness of natural-language documentation for formal libraries.
